title: The pages Directory Deep Dive
description: Understand exactly how files inside the pages folder become routes and what you can put there.

slides.title: The Heart of Routing ❤️
slides.content:
# pages/ is the Router

Every file you create inside the `pages/` directory automatically becomes a route – no configuration needed.

* The file **name** becomes the URL path.
* The **default export** must be a React component.
* Works with `.js`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`.

It's like a tree of routes mirroring your file system. 🌳

slides.title: Basic Pages Example (pages/index.js)
Adding More Pages (pages/contact.js)
slides.content: Just create a new file. It becomes `/contact`.

quizData.question: What URL will `pages/team.js` create?
quizData.explanation: The file name (minus extension) becomes the route. `team.js` → `/team`.

slides.title: What About Folders? 📁
slides.content:
# Folders Create Nested Routes

* `pages/blog.js` → `/blog`
* `pages/blog/first-post.js` → `/blog/first-post`

Nested folders automatically create nested URL segments. You don't need a router config file.

The **entire folder path** relative to `pages/` becomes the URL path.

quizData.question: A file at `pages/products/electronics/laptops.js` maps to which URL?
quizData.explanation: The full folder structure from `pages/` is translated directly into the URL path.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: You **cannot** have a file named `api` inside `pages` (like `pages/api.js`) because `pages/api` is a reserved folder for API routes. Next.js will treat it as an API folder, not a page.
